figures.label: Cp of the floated synthetic hull
figures.roundTrip: an input of the synthetic hull (hull.dims), from the same Day Table 2 row: this checks the hull generator reproduces it, not the model against a source

figures.label: Cm of the floated synthetic hull
figures.roundTrip: an input of the synthetic hull (hull.dims), from the same Day Table 2 row: this checks the hull generator reproduces it, not the model against a source

figures.label: BWL as floated
figures.roundTrip: an input of the synthetic hull (hull.dims), from the same Day Table 2 row: this checks the hull generator reproduces it, not the model against a source

figures.label: Tc as floated
figures.work: Day's row doesn't close on itself: LWL·BWL·Tc·Cp·Cm = 3.81·1.1087·0.0943·0.552·0.757 = 0.1665 m³ against 160 kg / 1025 = 0.1561 m³ (6.6% over). Floated at 160 kg with his Cp and Cm, the hull must come out about 6% shallower, hence ±8%
figures.roundTrip: Tc is an input too; the floated value differs only because Day's row doesn't close on its own displacement, so this checks the generator's closure, not the model

figures.label: Draft, board down
figures.work: Tc 0.094 + board 0.68 = 0.774 (the board's 680 mm is measured from the keel line)

polar.note: Day's own VPP, not measured speeds: a check that two VPPs agree, not that either is right. The PN (1102) is a relative handicap and gives no absolute speed, so it is recorded, not compared.

planing.note: A Laser planes on a reach in a breeze; the regime must say so and carry the planing model's flags.
planing.speedNote: ESTIMATED target, no measured or published figure was fetched: a Laser race report (afloat.ie, Howth) is quoted in search results as GPS trackers showing 'over 14 knots can readily be achieved on reaches' in gusty wind of unstated strength, and dinghy sailors' forum reports put a broad reach at 65–100% of the true wind. 12 kn at 16 kn true, ±25% (9–15 kn), is a band to see drift in, not a validation.

disagreements.used: 160 kg, Cp, Cm and BWL; Tc follows (0.089 m as floated against Day's 0.094)

published.estimatedWhy: Mast and daggerboard positions are lofilobzik's inferences from a diagram ILCA calls 'only a guide'; the boom height (BAS 0.57 m: gooseneck 945 mm above the butt, butt 0.375 m below deck) depends on a guessed butt depth; freeboard is a visual estimate; the rudder's span reading is ambiguous.
